problems.title: Magnetic Field Penetration
problems.statement: A semi-infinite superconductor occupies the region $x>0$. A magnetic field of $B_0 = 20\,\mathrm{mT}$ is applied at its surface. The field inside the superconductor follows the London penetration profile $$B(x)=B_0 e^{-x/\lambda_L},$$ where $\lambda_L = 50\,\mathrm{nm}$. At what depth $x$ is the magnetic field reduced to $1\%$ of its surface value?
problems.solution: We require $$B(x)=0.01B_0.$$ Using $$B(x)=B_0e^{-x/\lambda_L},$$ we obtain $$0.01=e^{-x/\lambda_L}.$$ Taking the natural logarithm, $$\ln(0.01)=-\frac{x}{\lambda_L}.$$ Therefore, $$x=-\lambda_L\ln(0.01).$$ Substituting $\lambda_L=50\,\mathrm{nm}$, $$x=-50\ln(0.01)\approx 50\times4.605\approx230\,\mathrm{nm}.$$ Hence the correct answer is $230\,\mathrm{nm}$.

problems.title: Magnetic Field in a Finite Superconducting Film
problems.statement: A superconducting film occupies the region $0\lt x\lt d$, with $d=100\,\mathrm{nm}$. The magnetic field inside the film is along the $z$-direction and satisfies the London equation $\frac{d^2B}{dx^2}=\frac{B}{\lambda_L^2}$, where $\lambda_L=50\,\mathrm{nm}$. The magnetic fields at the two surfaces are $B(0)=20\,\mathrm{mT}$ and $B(d)=5\,\mathrm{mT}$. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at $x=50\,\mathrm{nm}$?
problems.solution: The general solution of the London equation is $$B(x)=A\cosh\left(\frac{x}{\lambda_L}\right)+C\sinh\left(\frac{x}{\lambda_L}\right).$$ From the boundary condition at $x=0$, $$B(0)=A=20\,\mathrm{mT}.$$ Therefore, $$B(x)=20\cosh\left(\frac{x}{50}\right)+C\sinh\left(\frac{x}{50}\right),$$ where lengths are in nm. Using $B(100)=5\,\mathrm{mT}$, $$5=20\cosh(2)+C\sinh(2).$$ Hence $$C=\frac{5-20\cosh(2)}{\sinh(2)}\approx-19.37\,\mathrm{mT}.$$ At $x=50\,\mathrm{nm}$, $$B(50)=20\cosh(1)-19.37\sinh(1).$$ Evaluating, $$B(50)\approx8.10\,\mathrm{mT}.$$ Therefore the correct answer is $8.1\,\mathrm{mT}$.
